cell.condition_text: Meals and other food and beverages: itemization required only once a legislative agent's calendar-year spending for a particular covered official exceeds $50 (with specified exceptions for certain meetings).

instantiated_cells.justification: Section 101.73(B)(3) requires a legislative agent to report specified details for meal/food/beverage expenditures to a particular covered official only when, added to prior such payments in the same calendar year, they exceed a total of fifty dollars.

unscoreable_emissions.reason: The bundled Ohio lobbying provisions (§101.70-.79; §121.60-.69; §101.90-.98) define who is a legislative agent/executive agency lobbyist/retirement system lobbyist based on qualitative 'main purposes'/'regular and substantial basis' standards, but they do not set any dollar compensation threshold for when registration is required.
The bundled text requires registration within ten days following an engagement (§101.72(A); §121.62(A); §101.92(A)) and does not provide any expenditure-dollar threshold that triggers registration.

The statute defines lobbyists as individuals who actively advocate as one of their 'main purposes' or on a 'regular and substantial basis' (§101.70(F); §121.60(H); §101.90(H)) but gives no numeric time-percentage threshold.

The bundled statute requires expenditure statements with updated registration statements (§101.73(A); §101.72(B)) and contains no overall de minimis dollar threshold below which a legislative agent may omit filing; the only dollar threshold present is a meal itemization trigger, not a filing trigger.

No provision in the bundled text creates a numeric time-percentage de minimis threshold that would exempt a lobbyist from filing; filing is tied to being a legislative agent/employer and to updated registration deadlines (§101.72(B); §101.73(A)).
